analysis:
All changed files are tests or test support under provider-swift/Tests/DarkbloomCLITests. None ships in the provider binary, so no production security behavior changes in this batch.

SandboxStatusTests.swift (head lines 78-100) adds a workDisks test. It checks that SandboxStatusView renders work disks, online/offline state, free bytes, per-platform slot counts and the add-on's detail text. These are add-on-reported display fields. The test decodes fixture JSON only and runs no commands. Rendering uses add-on-controlled strings, which TB-013/T-061 already treat as an add-on trust matter; the test adds no new surface.

SandboxTestSupport.swift (head lines 187-201) extends the FakeSandboxInstaller shell script generator with planStandardError and workDisks. The workDisks option only writes a comment header naming SandboxInstaller.diskOption. planStandardError is passed through quoted() before it is echoed to stderr. The fake installer is used only in temporary roots inside tests.

SandboxWorkDiskTests.swift is a new file (433 lines). Only the metadata and a truncated patch excerpt were supplied, with no body text unit. I could not examine its contents in full. From the excerpt it exercises the new `darkbloom sandbox setup --disk` option: absolute-path normalisation, ownership-enabled APFS volume checks, and a plan with a disks array.

A gap for the next pass: the production implementations (SandboxWorkDisk, SandboxInstaller.diskOption, Sandbox.Setup options) are not in this batch. They are the real attack surface. These include passing user-chosen disk paths to the installer that runs as the Mac's owner (TB-013/T-061), path normalisation, symlink handling, volume ownership validation, and the plan-event JSON parsing of add-on output. Their review should cover path or argument injection and whether the disk-path checks hold. This batch gives no evidence of a regression, but it is not a clearance of that code, hence needs_deeper_review.
